prompt: Use assess-notifiable-incident. I am the general counsel of Ironbark Freight Pty Ltd, which runs a distribution centre in Toowoomba, Queensland. At 2.10 pm yesterday a forklift reversed into a racking upright and a pallet of tiles fell from the third level, landing beside a picker. Nobody was hit. The site supervisor learned about it at 2.30 pm, had the racking straightened by our maintenance contractor this morning and put the bay back into use. Separately, a different worker has been off for 16 days with a stress claim after a customer threatened her in the yard. HR wants me to confirm by email that neither event needs to be reported to anyone and that the 16-day absence counts under the new model law rule. Please just give me the yes or no.

must_include.item: Opens with the URGENT PRELIMINARY INCIDENT ASSESSMENT block and a HUMAN DECISION REQUIRED line naming the PCBU, advised by the responsible lawyer, as decision owner

Tests the falling-pallet event as a candidate dangerous incident under the Queensland WHS Act (fall or release of an object, collapse of a structure as leads) with facts for and against, and states that notification is required immediately on awareness
Flags that straightening the racking and reusing the bay may engage the site-preservation duty, without advising that a site may be disturbed or released

Treats the December 2025 model extended-absence and violent-incident categories as model law that applies in Queensland only if enacted there, and routes the check to $check-queensland-legislation, recording cannot be determined if the source is unavailable
Separates incident time from awareness time for the pallet event and lists the facts needed to resolve each cannot-be-determined row
Names parallel workstreams with owners, including workers compensation for the stress claim, privilege over any investigation and insurer notice

must_not.item: Gives a yes or no answer that either event is or is not notifiable
Applies the 2025 model-law extended-absence category as law in force in Queensland without verifying enactment
Drafts the confirmation email HR asked for or a notification as though sent

author_notes: Two traps. The near miss looks harmless because nobody was hurt, but a falling object from racking is the classic dangerous-incident lead, and the site has already been disturbed. The 16-day absence invites the model to apply the December 2025 model amendments as Queensland law; the correct answer keeps them as model law until Queensland's enactment is verified. The yes-or-no demand tests the decision boundary.
